A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite the method renaming and presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral-embedding approximation experiments, runtime measurements, NUMAP evaluations, and a time-series simulation, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional benchmark evaluations, quantitative ablations, and time-series comparisons.

M1.justification: GrEASE is renamed Sep-SpectralNet, but Algorithms 1–2 retain the same training, minibatch averaging, diagonalization, and inference procedure. NUMAP already included a second network and residual connections. v2 makes their formulation explicit; the reported network-width and embedding-size revisions are experimental configuration changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST and FashionMNIST to NUMAP evaluation in Appendix F, Tables 9–10, extending coverage to handwritten digits and fashion images. The earlier datasets, spectral-embedding tasks, synthetic examples, and time-series scenario remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds NUMAP-FT to the real-data quantitative comparisons, a NUMAP variant without residual connections to the CIFAR10 comparison, and P. UMAP to the time-series comparison in Figure 11. NUMAP-FT corresponds to the fine-tuning approach already illustrated on toy data in v1. NUMAP-SN remains in the appendices rather than being removed.

E3.justification: Appendix G changes the stated first hidden-layer width of the spectral networks from 128 to 256 and NUMAP's SE dimensions from 20 to 10 for CIFAR10 and 10 to 5 for Appliances. These are reported configuration revisions, not evidence that every retained experiment was rerun. The 80/20 split and principal evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 included the NUMAP-SN comparison and a qualitative fine-tuning learning-rate study. v2 substantially strengthens component validation with quantitative NUMAP-FT comparisons and residual-connection ablations in Appendix E, Tables 4–7. These test whether direct fine-tuning preserves both structures and whether residual connections specifically benefit global preservation.

E5.justification: The main NUMAP comparisons change from five reported runs to ten. v2 additionally specifies ten distinct seeds and independent t-tests for the GS comparisons, reporting p-values in Table 3. Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting already existed, and the stated repetition counts for SE approximation and scalability remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The NUMAP results are substantially revised and expanded. For example, CIFAR10 NUMAP mean GS changes from 0.089 to 0.054 under revised settings and run counts, so this is not an isolated same-setting gain. New benchmark and ablation results include MNIST kNN accuracy of 0.758 for NUMAP versus 0.801 for P. UMAP. The SE approximation values in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 8 remain identical.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and its proof, the complexity reasoning, graph construction, and Grassmann Score definitions remain substantively unchanged. The explicit UMAP loss and residual expression in v2 explain the existing procedure rather than introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim scalable, generalizable SE with separated eigenvectors, its application to generalizable UMAP, and a Grassmann-based global-structure evaluation measure. v2 emphasizes the SpectralNet connection and reorganizes the contribution list without materially changing these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive interpretations of the new ablations: NUMAP-FT's excellent Wine GS comes with poor local preservation, while residual connections principally improve global preservation. The conclusion adds alternative inputs to the UMAP-loss network as future work. Earlier discussions of catastrophic forgetting and GS's limited attention to local structure remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents SE dimensions for the synthetic examples and added image benchmarks, adds their sample and feature counts, and clarifies the residual connections and loss. Appendix G also revises the stated network configurations. Existing code links, hardware information, graph construction, and learning-rate policy remain available.

R1.justification: v2 expands diffusion-application citations, adds Damrich et al. on contrastive visualization methods, and explains why ICA/VARIMAX rotations do not recover the desired eigenvectors. It removes the graph-transformer references. The central positioning as an extension of SpectralNet and the taxonomy of competing SE approaches remain.

P1.justification: The method is renamed throughout, with revisions to the abstract, introduction, explanations, and captions. Section 5.3 separates local and global evaluation discussions, and the earlier fine-tuning appendix is incorporated into a consolidated ablation appendix. The main section order and much of the technical exposition are retained.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially reorganized: v1's combined Table 2 becomes separate local/global tables and expanded appendix comparisons. Figure 1 is repartitioned, its Banknote comparison is presented separately, and Figures 10–11 add multi-dataset and temporal comparison panels. The TMLR format also changes typography, title layout, and figure/table placement.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports NUMAP's design through quantitative fine-tuning and residual ablations, broader benchmark coverage, and explicit significance testing. These additions make the evidence more informative. The gain is tempered by insufficient qualification of broad preservation claims: Table 9 shows lower NUMAP kNN accuracy on both added image datasets, and Table 3 reports GS p-values of 0.118 and 0.056 for Wine and Banknote. The core SE theory and approximation evidence remain essentially unchanged.
